answer: We resist Sybil attacks by requiring peer-bonded stakes and random multi-agent auditing over graph partitions. When an identity cluster attempts expansion across a topological cut, independent auditors cross-examine every network bridge. Dishonest coordinates face immediate stake slashing, collapsing attacker payoffs from their expected zenith down to a ruined knoll. This enforces superlinear attacker cost as forging verified trust edges scales combinatorially.
